The es2 arpc_in_callback: copies only sizeof(*resp) (fixed size) — safe. The check at 1046 requires actual_length >= sizeof(*resp) then memcpy(rpc->resp, resp, sizeof(*resp)) — fixed-size copy from the URB buffer which is at least actual_length... wait, memcpy reads sizeof(*resp) bytes from resp — actual_length >= sizeof(*resp) guarantees the HC wrote at least that many bytes into the buffer. Buffer is ARPC_IN_SIZE_MAX-sized. Safe.

cport_in_callback: actual_length < sizeof(*header) rejected; then greybus_data_rcvd(hd, cport_id, urb->transfer_buffer, urb->actual_length). In gb_connection_recv:
- size < sizeof(header) rejected (again).
- memcpy(&header, data, sizeof(header)) — ok.
- msg_size = le16_to_cpu(header.size); if (size < msg_size) rejected. So msg_size <= size <= 2048. 
- Response path: message_size = sizeof(header) + message->payload_size (locally known, allocated <= buffer_size_max); checks size > message_size → EMSGSIZE; size < message_size → short response allowed → message->payload_size = size - sizeof(*header) — this shrinks payload_size to actual received, then memcpy(message->buffer, data, size) where size == msg_size <= actual URB length. message->buffer was allocated with payload_size + header ≥ message_size ≥ size. So the copy is in-bounds both source and dest. Good.
- Request path: gb_operation_create_incoming: request_size = size - header; gb_operation_create_common → gb_operation_message_alloc checks message_size = request_size + header = size <= hd->buffer_size_max (2048, clamped to GB_OPERATION_MESSAGE_SIZE_MAX). If msg_size > 2048, allocation fails and message dropped. Then memcpy(operation->request->header, data, size) — dest allocated exactly message_size = size. In-bounds. Source read: data buffer is kmalloc(2048) and actual_length <= 2048 guaranteed by URB/HCD contract; msg_size <= size = actual_length. So source read within the URB transfer buffer of 2048.

So the primary es2.c:844 candidate appears SAFE: the invariant holds not via direct bound of actual_length against transfer_buffer_length, but (a) USB HCD contract bounds actual_length <= transfer_buffer_length (2048) — this is the local requested size, and HCD code guarantees it; (b) gb_connection_recv checks size >= header-parsed msg_size and msg_size (u16 from wire) is clamped by allocation-time check against hd->buffer_size_max.

Wait — but is actual_length guaranteed <= transfer_buffer_length? Yes, by USB core/HCD: urb->actual_length is set by the host controller driver to the number of bytes transferred into the buffer, never more than the buffer length. In mainline UHCI/OHCI/EHCI/xHCI, actual_length is bounded by the transfer length. A malicious *device* cannot cause actual_length > buffer size unless the HCD itself is buggy. The threat model here: device firmware (the greybus AP bridge module or a malicious USB device) sends more data. The HCD will only DMA into the allocated 2048-byte buffer; if the device sends more, either the transfer fails with -EOVERFLOW (babble) or data is discarded. In xHCI, bulk IN babble → stopped, actual_length reflects valid bytes. So actual_length ∈ [0, 2048].

Then all copies are bounded by msg_size. So no OOB.

But wait — check the response path more carefully. `message_size = sizeof(*header) + message->payload_size`. If `size > message_size` → errno = -EMSGSIZE → then `if (errno) size = sizeof(*header);` then memcpy(message->buffer, data, sizeof(header)) — fine. If size <= message_size: memcpy(message->buffer, data, size) — size ≤ message_size ≤ allocated buffer. Fine.

What about `gb_operation_short_response_allowed`? payload_size shrunk; copy still size ≤ message_size_new. Fine.
